assessment.nobel_worthiness: Exact, model-independent relations (fluctuation theorems, Jarzynski equality) that extend thermodynamics to small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems. This is the kind of simple, universal and rigorously provable result that explains a whole class of messy phenomena, and it gave a new language for molecular motors, colloids and single-molecule experiments.
assessment.attribution: Evans and co-workers (with Cohen and Morriss) gave the first fluctuation theorem, Jarzynski the work relation, Crooks the detailed fluctuation relation and Seifert the stochastic-thermodynamics framework. The supplied credit omits other pioneers such as Gallavotti and Cohen, Kurchan, Lebowitz and Spohn, so a three-person split is contestable. I would give Jarzynski, Evans and Seifert as the most defensible among the supplied names, with Crooks the main alternative.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The relations were tested in optical-tweezer RNA unfolding, colloidal and electronic single-electron experiments, and the framework is now textbook material. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority among Evans, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski, Crooks and Kurchan is not fully settled, and some of these people are not in the credited names.

Whether the committee regards this as physics-prize territory (statistical physics) rather than chemistry is a judgement call. My recollection of the experimental confirmations is from memory, not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introduced the Z2 topological classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators and the quantum spin Hall state. Together with the experimental demonstration in HgTe quantum wells, this opened the field of topological materials, with broad conceptual reach into band theory, spintronics and later topological superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the clear theory pioneers. Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental discovery, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and Fu-Kane work on 3D topological insulators, are not in the credited set, which leaves a real gap in a fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with ARPES on 3D materials and transport in several platforms. The effect is stable and widely used, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) lies outside the supplied names.
The 2D and 3D topological insulator stories may deserve a combined or different split. Practical applications remain limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases are a unifying mechanism: the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase appear in quantum mechanics, optics, molecular physics, Hall conductance and topological band theory. It is one of the clearest cases of a simple general idea that reorganised many subfields.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) established the geometric phase of gauge potentials, and Berry (1984) the adiabatic phase. Bohm died in 1992 and cannot be recognised, and others (Pancharatnam, Simon, Wilczek-Zee) contributed related ideas. Two living laureates give a clean and fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of experimental confirmation in electron interferometry, optics and condensed matter. If anything, recognition is late.
uncertainties: Posthumous exclusion of Bohm and the Pancharatnam precedent complicate the narrative.
Whether this is seen as one discovery or two related ones is debatable, and the committee may prefer a more recent application-driven topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The defect-mediated melting theory of two-dimensional matter, with the hexatic phase and its universal predictions, is a model of how a clean mechanism (dislocation and disclination unbinding) explains a phase transition without symmetry-breaking order. It follows the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless line already recognised in 2016, and is quantitatively tested in colloids, liquid crystals and simulations.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson developed the dislocation-mediated two-step melting theory, and Young contributed the independent elaboration of the dislocation-unbinding picture and numerical work. I would give the prize to Halperin and Nelson. The supplied credit does not include Kosterlitz and Thouless, who were already honoured, so the priority chain is clear. Young's role is real but secondary.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with experimental realisation in colloidal crystals and numerical confirmation, though the first-order versus continuous nature of 2D melting is system-dependent. Recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Simulations show the melting scenario depends on the particle interactions, so the universality claim is not absolute.
Halperin also appears in another candidate (anyon statistics in the fractional quantum Hall effect), which could affect allocation across prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory showed that flocks can have true long-range order in two dimensions, circumventing the Mermin-Wagner theorem through non-equilibrium effects. This is a foundational result for active matter, with universal scaling exponents, and it connects biology, soft matter and statistical physics.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek and co-workers introduced the minimal model (1995), and Toner and Tu gave the hydrodynamic theory and the exact exponent predictions (1995, 1998). The three supplied names map well onto a fair configuration. Ramaswamy and the Simha-Ramaswamy hydrodynamics of active suspensions are not credited, and may deserve mention.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature theoretically, with simulations and experiments on bacteria, colloids and animals, but quantitative experimental tests of the Toner-Tu exponents are limited. Perhaps somewhat early for a prize.
uncertainties: Direct experimental verification of the predicted scaling exponents is thin.
Credit relative to the wider active-matter community (Ramaswamy, Marchetti and others) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the exact infinite-dimensional limit of correlated lattice models and provides a controlled non-perturbative tool for the Mott transition and correlated materials. It brings a clean mean-field mechanism to a hard many-body problem, and DMFT plus electronic structure is a standard method.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit (1989), and Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping onto an impurity problem (1992). Metzner is not in the supplied credited names, so the allocation is incomplete. I would propose the three supplied names, noting the Metzner gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature theoretically and heavily used in materials science. The evidence is more in explaining and computing than in a single decisive experiment, so the case is methodological rather than a discovery.
uncertainties: Metzner's decisive contribution is outside the supplied credit, and the cluster extensions and quantitative accuracy for real materials remain debated.
A method-based prize is harder to define as a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recognition that in two dimensions particles can have fractional exchange statistics is a deep conceptual advance, underlying fractional quantum Hall states and topological quantum computation. It is a clean mechanism rooted in the topology of configuration space.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim (1977) established the possibility of intermediate statistics, and Wilczek (1982) coined anyons and gave the flux-charge construction. Wilczek is already a laureate, but nothing prevents a second prize. The three-person configuration is natural and reasonably fair.
assessment.maturity: Anyonic statistics has now been observed in quantum Hall interferometry and collision experiments (2020 onwards), which is timely, but the independent confirmation is recent and some interpretations are still being tested.
uncertainties: Experimental evidence is recent and may still be contested in detail, and a separate experimental candidate exists on the longlist.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for non-Abelian anyon evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the origin of primordial fluctuations, with the quantum-fluctuation seed of structure as a statistical-physics-like mechanism. Its predictions of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum agree well with CMB data, and it is one of the most influential ideas in cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario, Linde the new and chaotic inflation fixing its problems, and Mukhanov computed the quantum origin of structure. Starobinsky and Albrecht-Steinhardt are important omissions from the supplied credit, so allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Observationally supported by CMB and large-scale structure data, but the specific inflationary model and the decisive signature (primordial gravitational waves) are not confirmed. Arguably premature.
uncertainties: No direct detection of primordial B-modes, and alternatives are not fully excluded.
Starobinsky's priority and the Guth-Linde-Mukhanov split are disputed, and this is outside my field of expertise.
